annotations.description: Playing Thriving Isle before equipping Adventuring Gear to Oashra Cultivator means the landfall trigger fires while the equipment is unattached, wasting the +2/+2 bonus. The opponent has no untapped blockers, so a 2/5 Oashra Cultivator could have attacked for 2 free damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Thriving Isle first, before equipping Adventuring Gear
annotations.betterLine: Equip Adventuring Gear to Oashra Cultivator for {1}, then play Thriving Isle to trigger landfall, making Oashra Cultivator a 2/5 that can attack unblocked for 2 damage.

annotations.description: Declined to equip Adventuring Gear to Oashra Cultivator before combat. The opponent's board is entirely tapped or summoning sick, so Oashra Cultivator could attack unblocked. Equipping for {1} and attacking would deal 2 damage for free (or more if the +2/+2 landfall buff is active this turn from Thriving Isle entering). This costs only 1 mana with no meaningful alternative use for that mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without equipping Adventuring Gear, missing a free attack opportunity.
annotations.betterLine: Equip Adventuring Gear to Oashra Cultivator for {1}, then attack for 2 damage into an empty/tapped board.

annotations.description: Blocked a 2/5 Oashra Cultivator (buffed by Adventuring Gear landfall) with a 2/1 Sage's Row Savant. The Savant dies without killing the Cultivator. At 20 life, taking 2 damage is very affordable, and the Savant could have provided future value as an attacker or blocker.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Oashra Cultivator with Sage's Row Savant, trading the 2/1 for nothing (Cultivator survives at 2/3)
annotations.betterLine: Don't block, take 2 damage (go to 18 life), keep Sage's Row Savant for future attacks or blocks. The Savant's 2 power could be relevant for racing or trading with a more important creature later.

annotations.description: Timed out and passed the entire precombat main phase without taking any action. Missed playing Evolving Wilds (free land drop), which could be cracked for landfall on Adventuring Gear, and missed casting Turntimber Basilisk (2/1 deathtouch) which was castable with available mana and would be an excellent answer to Merrow Reejerey. The opponent is building a Merfolk board with unblockable damage, and doing nothing for a full turn is devastating.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and passed priority, taking no actions during the main phase.
annotations.betterLine: Play Evolving Wilds, crack it to fetch a Forest (triggering Adventuring Gear landfall), then cast Turntimber Basilisk with the 3 green mana available. This develops the board with a deathtouch creature to threaten blocking Merrow Reejerey.

annotations.description: Blocked a 0/3 Oashra Cultivator with the valuable Merrow Reejerey (2/2 lord). The block prevents 0 damage (Cultivator has 0 power) and doesn't kill the Cultivator (2 damage vs 3 toughness). The block accomplishes literally nothing while exposing the Reejerey to potential combat tricks from the opponent's 5-card hand, and the opponent has Adventuring Gear on the battlefield which could be relevant.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Oashra Cultivator (0/3) with Merrow Reejerey (2/2)
annotations.betterLine: Don't block. Take 0 damage from the 0-power creature and keep Merrow Reejerey safe from any potential combat tricks.

annotations.description: Cast Turntimber Basilisk before playing Evolving Wilds. Lands should generally be played before spells to maximize flexibility. Playing Evolving Wilds first costs nothing (it enters tapped, doesn't affect available mana for the Basilisk cast) but ensures the land is on the battlefield in case something unexpected happens during spell resolution.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Turntimber Basilisk before playing the land drop (Evolving Wilds)
annotations.betterLine: Play Evolving Wilds first, then cast Turntimber Basilisk with the same 3 untapped lands. The end board state is identical but proper sequencing preserves maximum flexibility.

annotations.description: Failed to activate Evolving Wilds in postcombat main phase. With Drownyard Explorers in hand costing {3}{U}, cracking Evolving Wilds now (fetching an Island or Forest) would ensure having exactly 4 lands untapped next turn to cast it on curve. The fetched land enters tapped, so doing it now costs nothing. Saving Evolving Wilds for a future landfall trigger with Adventuring Gear is speculative since the gear isn't even equipped yet.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Evolving Wilds, ending the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Evolving Wilds to fetch a basic land (likely Island for blue mana), ensuring 4 mana available next turn to cast Drownyard Explorers on curve, which also creates a Clue token advancing the Mechanized Production / Gearseeker Serpent artifact synergy plan.

annotations.description: By casting Exclusion Mage first (non-Merfolk, doesn't trigger Reejerey), Qwen3 Valley misses the line of casting Vodalian Arcanist first (a Merfolk, triggering Reejerey to untap an Island), which would provide enough mana to cast both Vodalian Arcanist AND Exclusion Mage, and then tap Vodalian Arcanist for {C} to also cast Opt. Instead, only Exclusion Mage + Opt can be cast this turn, missing deploying an extra 1/3 body.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Exclusion Mage first, which doesn't trigger Merrow Reejerey, limiting the turn to Exclusion Mage + Opt (2 spells, 1 creature deployed).
annotations.betterLine: Cast Vodalian Arcanist ({1}{U}) → Reejerey untaps an Island → Cast Exclusion Mage ({2}{U}) bouncing Turntimber Basilisk → Tap Vodalian Arcanist for {C} → Cast Opt. This deploys 2 creatures, bounces the Basilisk, and draws a card — getting significantly more value from 4 lands.

annotations.description: Exclusion Mage's ETB trigger is bouncing Oashra Cultivator (a 0/3 that ramps) instead of Turntimber Basilisk (a 2/1 with deathtouch and landfall-based forced blocking). The Basilisk is the much more dangerous creature — it has deathtouch which trades with any creature, and its landfall ability can force Qwen3's creatures to block it, potentially killing key pieces like Merrow Reejerey. The opponent has Evolving Wilds to trigger landfall. Oashra Cultivator is a 0/3 that costs mana to activate and is relatively low-impact. Bouncing the Basilisk would remove the primary threat and force the opponent to re-invest 3 mana (1GG) to replay it, while bouncing Oashra Cultivator only sets back a 1-mana ramp creature.
annotations.actionTaken: Bounced Oashra Cultivator with Exclusion Mage's ETB
annotations.betterLine: Bounce Turntimber Basilisk — it's the bigger threat with deathtouch and a landfall ability that can force unfavorable blocks, especially with Evolving Wilds available to trigger landfall.

annotations.description: Passed the turn without casting Vodalian Arcanist, the only available play. Vodalian Arcanist is a Merfolk that would get +1/+1 from Merrow Reejerey (becoming a 2/4), trigger Reejerey's tap/untap ability, and provide a mana ability for future instant/sorcery casting. With exactly {1}{U} available and no instant-speed plays to hold up, there is zero reason not to deploy it.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority in postcombat main phase, ending the turn with 2 unspent mana and an uncast creature.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Vodalian Arcanist for {1}{U}, getting a 2/4 Merfolk (with Reejerey buff), triggering Reejerey to tap/untap a permanent, and adding another attacker/blocker to the board.

annotations.description: Timed out and passed the entire precombat main phase at 10 life with no creatures, facing 4 damage per turn (including 2 unblockable). Had 5 untapped lands and multiple castable spells including Drownyard Explorers (2/4 body + Clue token) and Oashra Cultivator, plus Evolving Wilds activation available.
annotations.actionTaken: No response (timeout) — passed the turn without casting anything or activating any abilities.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Drownyard Explorers for {3}{U} to get a 2/4 blocker and a Clue token, then cast Oashra Cultivator with remaining green mana for another body, and activate Evolving Wilds to fetch a land. This deploys desperately needed blockers and advances the board.

annotations.description: Cast Storm Sculptor before playing the Island from hand. With 6 lands and Merrow Reejerey's untap trigger from casting the Merfolk spell, Qwen3 would have had 3 mana remaining after Sculptor instead of 2, allowing them to replay Triton Shorestalker AND cast Vodalian Arcanist (another body) in the same turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Storm Sculptor with only 5 lands in play, before making the land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island first, then cast Storm Sculptor (triggering Reejerey to untap a land for 3 remaining mana), bounce Triton Shorestalker, replay Shorestalker (1 mana), and cast Vodalian Arcanist (2 mana) — deploying maximum board presence while still attacking for 4 unblockable.

annotations.description: Merrow Reejerey is already untapped, so targeting it with its own tap/untap trigger accomplishes nothing. By untapping a tapped Island instead, Qwen3 Valley would have had 2 untapped Islands, then playing the Island from hand would give 3 mana — enough to cast Vodalian Arcanist (1U), which is itself a Merfolk that would trigger Reejerey again, potentially chaining into further plays like Aquatic Incursion.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted the already-untapped Merrow Reejerey with its own trigger, wasting the tap/untap ability.
annotations.betterLine: Untap a tapped Island to gain extra mana, then play Island from hand for 3 available mana, cast Vodalian Arcanist (triggering Reejerey again to untap another Island), potentially chaining into Aquatic Incursion or holding up Soul Read.

annotations.description: Declined Merrow Reejerey's tap/untap trigger when casting Storm Sculptor. Untapping a tapped Island would have given an extra mana, potentially enabling recasting Triton Shorestalker (bounced by Storm Sculptor) for additional value and another Reejerey trigger.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined the Merrow Reejerey trigger (chose not to tap or untap any permanent).
annotations.betterLine: Untap a tapped Island to have 2 mana available, then after Storm Sculptor bounces Triton Shorestalker, recast it for 1 mana, triggering Reejerey again for further untaps and board development.

annotations.description: Cracking Evolving Wilds now wastes a potential landfall trigger for Adventuring Gear. With no creatures on board to equip, the landfall is meaningless right now. Saving Evolving Wilds for a turn when a creature is equipped with Adventuring Gear would grant +2/+2, which could be significant for racing or blocking against the unblockable threats.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Evolving Wilds during opponent's turn with no creatures on board to benefit from Adventuring Gear landfall
annotations.betterLine: Save Evolving Wilds for a future turn when a creature is equipped with Adventuring Gear to get a +2/+2 landfall trigger. The extra mana from fetching now is marginal since the land enters tapped anyway.

annotations.description: Cracking Evolving Wilds while no creature is equipped with Adventuring Gear wastes the landfall trigger. The fetched land enters tapped so it doesn't enable anything extra this turn. Saving Evolving Wilds for a future turn when a creature is equipped with Adventuring Gear would provide a surprise +2/+2 combat trick at instant speed, which is significant value given Llama4 Sport is at 10 life facing unblockable threats.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Evolving Wilds in response to Storm Sculptor on the stack, wasting the Adventuring Gear landfall trigger.
annotations.betterLine: Save Evolving Wilds for a future turn when a creature is equipped with Adventuring Gear to get a meaningful +2/+2 landfall trigger. The mana is not needed this turn since 4 untapped lands suffice for Drownyard Explorers.

annotations.description: With a very blue-heavy hand (Drownyard Explorers 3U, Gearseeker Serpent 5UU, Mechanized Production 2UU), fetching Forest instead of Island makes blue mana tighter. With Forest, casting Mechanized Production (2UU) requires both Island and Thriving Isle committed to blue, leaving no flexibility. An Island would provide a third blue source for more reliable casting of multiple blue-heavy spells.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched Forest with Oashra Cultivator
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Island to better support the blue-heavy hand (Gearseeker Serpent, Mechanized Production, Drownyard Explorers)

annotations.description: Bouncing Storm Sculptor with its own ETB trigger wastes 4 mana entirely, leaving no new creature on board. The opponent is at 10 life and Qwen3 Valley has unblockable threats - keeping the 4/3 unblockable Storm Sculptor on board alongside Triton Shorestalker would create massive pressure.
annotations.actionTaken: Bounced Storm Sculptor with its own ETB, wasting 4 mana and gaining nothing.
annotations.betterLine: Bounce Triton Shorestalker (1-drop), then replay it for U, triggering Merrow Reejerey's tap/untap ability. This keeps the 4/3 unblockable Storm Sculptor on board while only temporarily losing the Shorestalker, which can be immediately replayed.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 6 life with all lands tapped. Casting Shaper Apprentice (2 mana) and Vodalian Arcanist (2 mana) would trigger Merrow Reejerey twice, allowing tapping down both of opponent's potential blockers (Drownyard Explorers and Oashra Cultivator). Then attacking with all four creatures — Shorestalker (2), Reejerey (2), Shaper Apprentice (3/2 flying), Arcanist (2/4) — deals 9 unblocked damage for lethal. Storm Sculptor costs 4 mana, requires bouncing a creature, and doesn't set up lethal.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Storm Sculptor, which bounces own creature and doesn't enable lethal this turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Shaper Apprentice (1U) then Vodalian Arcanist (1U), using both Reejerey triggers to tap Drownyard Explorers and Oashra Cultivator, then attack with all four creatures for 9 damage — lethal against 6 life.

annotations.description: Qwen3 Valley used the Merrow Reejerey trigger to 'untap' Merrow Reejerey, which was already untapped, wasting the trigger entirely. Untapping a tapped Island would have given them an additional mana, potentially enabling further plays this turn (like casting Shaper Apprentice after Storm Sculptor resolves, which would chain another Reejerey trigger).
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted the already-untapped Merrow Reejerey with its own tap/untap trigger, accomplishing nothing.
annotations.betterLine: Untap a tapped Island to gain an additional mana, enabling potential follow-up plays like casting Shaper Apprentice (1U) or Vodalian Arcanist (1U) after Storm Sculptor resolves and bounces a creature.

annotations.description: At 6 life facing Triton Shorestalker (unblockable, 2/2) and Merrow Reejerey (2/2), the player failed to block Merrow Reejerey with Drownyard Explorers 2/4, which would have killed Reejerey and kept Explorers alive. Instead, the chosen block ID (p65) doesn't match any valid blocker, likely resulting in no valid block. This means taking 4 damage (to 2 life) instead of 2 damage (to 4 life) while also removing a key lord creature.
annotations.actionTaken: Selected an invalid or non-existent blocker (p65), likely resulting in no block on Merrow Reejerey
annotations.betterLine: Block Merrow Reejerey with Drownyard Explorers 2/4 — Explorers survives at 2 toughness remaining while killing the 2/2 Reejerey, and you only take 2 unblockable damage instead of 4 total.

annotations.description: Declined Merrow Reejerey's 'may tap or untap target permanent' trigger, which is a free ability with no downside. Could have untapped an Island to hold up mana or untapped Triton Shorestalker/Merrow Reejerey as potential blockers. With the opponent at 2 life and having 4 cards in hand (potential interaction), having even 1 mana open or an untapped creature provides value at no cost.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined the Merrow Reejerey trigger, untapping nothing.
annotations.betterLine: Use the trigger to untap an Island (for potential mana) or untap a creature like Merrow Reejerey for blocking, since it's pure upside.

annotations.description: At 2 life, Llama4 Sport killed Shaper Apprentice instead of Merrow Reejerey. Triton Shorestalker is an unblockable 2/2 (buffed by Merrow Reejerey) and deals exactly lethal next turn. Killing Merrow Reejerey would have reduced Shorestalker to 1/1 (only 1 unblockable damage) and Shaper Apprentice to 2/1 (blockable by Drownyard Explorers), allowing survival at 1 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Shaper Apprentice with Master's Rebuke, leaving the unblockable Triton Shorestalker as a buffed 2/2 — lethal next turn.
annotations.betterLine: Target Merrow Reejerey with Master's Rebuke. Without the lord, Triton Shorestalker becomes 1/1 (1 unblockable damage) and Shaper Apprentice becomes 2/1 (blockable by Drownyard Explorers 2/4), allowing survival at 1 life.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 2 life and Triton Shorestalker (2/2 unblockable) is on board ready to attack for lethal. Casting Aquatic Incursion before combat is unnecessary and gives the opponent a window to potentially interact (though their lands are tapped). The correct play when you have guaranteed lethal is to proceed directly to combat.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Aquatic Incursion in precombat main phase before attacking for lethal
annotations.betterLine: Skip directly to combat and attack with Triton Shorestalker for 2 unblockable damage to win the game. Cast nothing precombat when lethal is already on board.
